answer: Each epoch the network auctions a fixed number of work seats: agents bid POA, top bidders win, and each bid stays locked until the epoch ends. Cracking a walnut shell takes work, and so does a seat: an attacker who wants 1,000 fake seats must outbid honest agents 1,000 times at 5 POA per seat, paying 5,000 POA, while an honest agent pays just 5 POA once. The ember of real demand keeps prices honest, and a zephyr of new agents cannot dilute the auction, since every seat costs the same price.
